research_question: Can blood-cell-inspired dynamic intravascular obstacles be added as an optional, default-off environment feature that moves with the local flow and records robot-obstacle interaction, without perturbing legacy runs?
main_variable: dynamic_intravascular_particles flag (obstacle presence only). No reward, physics-of-robots or action-semantics change; obstacles exert a separation impulse, not a reward penalty.

model.advection: tree.flow with the same occluded-radius override the robots see (one flow model for both)
model.drift: small random drift scaled to the local flow speed (lateral tumbling proxy)
model.containment: projected back into the lumen every step like a robot
model.size: radius_ratio (default 1.6) x robot_radius -- dimensionless, follows device scale
model.scope_statement: First-version geometric model. NOT a red-blood-cell model: no haemorheology, no deformability, no near-wall lift, no rouleaux. 'Blood-cell-inspired' is the honest ceiling of the claim.

records.persistence: state_dict round-trips particle state and its dedicated RNG

invariants.legacy_default: flag off reproduces legacy behaviour bit-identically; dedicated particle RNG leaves the env's own RNG stream untouched even when enabled

validation.pytest: tests/test_dynamic_particles.py: displacement aligns with local flow (mean cos > 0.8), lumen containment, dimensionless size, RNG stream preservation, flag-off bit-identity, info records, separation impulse at exact overlap, state round-trip
validation.smoke: scripts/run_scaling_smokes.sh dynamic_obstacles: 448 transitions with 16 particles, PPO update finite

performance_claim: none: impact on success/collision rates requires new training runs with the flag enabled
